venue.name: McMillan Arts Centre - The MAC
venue.description: The McMillan Arts Centre, known locally as the MAC, is the community arts centre for the Parksville and Qualicum Beach area, owned by the Oceanside Community Arts Council. It occupies the old Parksville School, a 1913 building on McMillan Street, and holds exhibition galleries, a gift shop carrying work by more than 180 local artists, a box office for events around Oceanside, a studio used by the MAC School for the Creative Arts, and a 4,000 square foot community garden at the back. The MAC School runs art classes for adults, seniors and children, including a weekly Creative Kids after school club and a summer programme of short classes and camps. Nothing on the site is written for school or daycare group bookings.
venue.hours_notes: Tuesday through Sunday, 11 am to 3 pm. Closed Mondays. The gift shop keeps the same hours, and online orders are collected Tuesday to Saturday between 11 am and 3 pm.
venue.seasonal_notes: Exhibitions change monthly across the Concert, Oceanside and Nemeth galleries, and the schedule for the whole year is published in advance with hang dates and reception dates. The Creative Kids summer programme of short classes and camps runs in July and August, and the after school club runs weekly through the autumn.
venue.price_year_or_season: Class prices read on 7 September 2026 from the shop listings then live. The summer 2026 Creative Kids classes described on the MAC School page have already finished and are no longer in the shop.

programs.name: Visit the galleries and gift shop
programs.description: A walk in visit to the MAC's exhibition galleries and its gift shop. The building holds the Concert Gallery, the Oceanside Gallery and the Nemeth Gallery, and the exhibition schedule changes monthly, with the year's hang and reception dates published in advance. Artists in residence work in the building on most days it is open, and the Nemeth Gallery has shown work by the Creative Kids classes. The gift shop sells cards, jewellery, glass, pottery, textiles, wood and prints by local artists. No admission price is published, and nothing on the site describes a booking route or a rate for a school or daycare group.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through the three galleries to look at the paintings, textiles, glass and pottery on show, and watch an artist in residence working on a day when one is in.
programs.our_note: They open at 11 and close at 3, Tuesday to Sunday, which is a narrow window for a morning outing and no use at all on a Monday. Nothing on their site is written for children's groups, so ring first and ask what a group of small children can actually do while they are there.
programs.practical_summary: It is a 1913 schoolhouse and the site says nothing about washrooms, a room to eat in, or where a bus can stop. The community garden at the back of the building is open most of the day and is the obvious fallback for eating outside.
programs.evidence: It is a building, a venue, on McMillan St., in Parksville, that showcases the works of 2D, 3D and performance art.

programs.name: Creative Kids After School Art Club
programs.description: A weekly two hour art class in the MAC Studio on Thursday afternoons from 4 pm to 6 pm, for ages 7 to 15. Each week has a different project. The class opens with art games to loosen up, then a short lesson or explanation before the making starts, and over the term the children build confidence, try new materials and learn some fundamentals of art. Each date is bought separately in the online shop at $25 for one child for one session, and the maximum is 12 participants. This is a registration for an individual child, not a booking a group leader can make for a whole class, so a leader would have to buy one seat per child per date and would run out of places at 12.
programs.what_children_do: Play a short art game to warm up, listen to a quick explanation of the week's project, then work at a table in the studio on that piece, which one week is watercolour ocean silhouettes and another week something else.
programs.our_note: This is a drop off class families sign up for one week at a time, and it is not sold as a group booking. Twelve places is the hard cap, so a class of twenty will not fit even if you buy every seat. It starts at 4 pm, an hour after the building's public hours end.
programs.practical_summary: Two hours in the MAC Studio, 4 pm to 6 pm on Thursdays. Nothing is published about washrooms, snacks, or whether an adult stays with the child.
programs.payment_timing: Each date is paid for in full at the online shop checkout when the place is booked.

programs.name: Creative Kids summer classes and art camps
programs.description: More than forty two hour art classes across July and August, running morning and afternoon, plus three art camps. The classes are held in the MAC Community Art Garden at the back of the building. A child can take a morning class and an afternoon class on the same day and stay through the lunch hour for $10 extra, which makes a 10 am to 3 pm day. The summer these dates describe has finished and the listings have come off the shop, so the price of a single class, the ages each one takes and the dates of the camps are not currently published anywhere on the site. The separate Creative Kids Under Five collection is empty at the moment.
programs.our_note: The summer this describes has already been and gone, so read it as a guide to what they usually run rather than as something you can book. The $10 lunch hour charge is the part worth remembering if you are stringing a morning and an afternoon class together. Ask them in the spring what next summer looks like and whether anything is coming back for the under fives.
programs.practical_summary: Classes happen outside in the community garden at the back of the building. Washrooms, cover if it rains and where the children eat are all unstated.
programs.extra_fees_note: Want to take a morning AND afternoon class? Bring your lunch and stay over the lunch hour ($10 extra) for a 10-3 day.
programs.evidence: We have over 40 2-hour art classes lined up for morning and afternoon during July and August

images.alt: A two storey blue wooden heritage building with white window trim and two outside staircases, seen across a lawn through overhanging green leaves.
A gallery room with white walls and a wood floor, six framed landscape photographs hung in a row, and a person sitting on a low wooden bench looking at them.
Seen from above, a child in an orange shirt passes a paintbrush across a white table to another child's hand, beside cups of yellow and red paint and scattered coloured pencils.

gaps: NO SCHOOL OR DAYCARE OFFERING IS PUBLISHED. Searching their own shop and pages for school group, field trip, daycare, preschool, class visit and group tour returned nothing but paintings and greeting cards with those words in the title. The children's classes here are individual registrations bought one seat and one date at a time in the online shop, not class bookings. Whether they would take a booked group at all is unanswered, so ask by phone.

The Creative Kids After School Art Club is capped at 12 participants and priced at $25 for one child for one session. That $25 is per child and it is a quote from the listing, not an inference. Read as a class fee it would look like a bargain for thirty children when in fact thirty seats do not exist.
no admission price for the galleries is published, and nothing says whether visiting is free.

youngest age welcomed is not stated. The after school club is ages 7 to 15 and the Creative Kids Under Five collection is currently empty, so there is nothing running for under fives that we could see.

washrooms, an indoor place to eat, rain cover, stroller access, wheelchair access and bus parking are all unstated. The room rentals page does mention access to a full kitchen, but that is written for people hiring a room.
capacity for a group visit to the galleries is not stated, and neither is a lead time or a booking route for one.
The Workshops and Classes page at /pages/workshops-classes is live but has no content on it beyond the heading.

The site's Open Graph image is the MAC wordmark logo rather than a photograph, so it was not used as the hero. The homepage banner is a painting of the building by Carla Flegel rather than a photo, so a photograph of the building from the About Us page was used instead.

The postal code is ambiguous. Their homepage prints V9P 2H5 under the street address, but their contact page gives V9P 2H5 as the code for their PO Box mailing address. The postal code has been left off the street address here.

The community garden at the back is a public 4,000 square foot fenced space open roughly 10 am to 6 pm seven days a week, but it is managed by the PQB Fruit Tree Project and its own workshop listings sit on that partner's website, so nothing about them has been recorded here.

The Art Therapy Open Studio runs Mondays 5 pm to 7 pm as a drop in, by donation, with supplies provided. Admission by donation is neither free nor a price, so no cost has been recorded, and Monday is a day the building is otherwise closed.

conflicts.note: Two different phone numbers for the same place. The map panel on their home page gives one, and their contact page and room rentals page both give the other. We use the contact page number. If it does not answer, try the other.
